text:
Bo Horvat left Saturday's game in Anaheim late, which gave the Islanders a scare, and was back Tuesday to extend his point streak to five games. The captain has 21 points in 20 games, 9 goals on 9.4 expected, so his scoring is about as honest as it gets.

The underlying change is in his own shooting. He's generating 1.35 expected goals per 60, up from 1.02 last season, and his scoring rate has climbed from 2.42 points per 60 to 3.00. That matters on a team whose record runs ahead of its chances: the Islanders' goaltending has been carrying a lot, and Horvat is one of the few regulars whose production comes from real looks.

Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 99th percentile last season, and it said his chances deserved more than his goals did. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the shape of it: 59% of his shots came off the rush, and he carries the puck in on 62% of his entries. Watch him in the first few seconds after the Islanders win the puck back.
